name: XRP Ledger
executive_summary: The XRP Ledger has been running since 2012, designed from the start for fast, low-cost cross-border payments rather than general-purpose computing, and fourteen years later at the time of this scoring that focus shows up in a Real-World Utility score of 86 and a TradFi score of 71. Real-world payment usage and TradFi rail access carry the score, while a small, curated set of roughly 35 validators and token supply that was mostly pre-mined at launch hold it back. The AI score of 65 reflects a ledger with rich built-in payment features but no ability to deploy custom code on top of it, a limitation that's been in place since launch.

key_findings: XRP's score is carried by two strengths -- real-world payment usage (86) and regulated institutional access (81) -- and held back by two weaknesses: token supply that was mostly created and allocated at launch rather than mined over time (64), and a validator set that's curated by a small group rather than open to anyone (46).

XRP Ledger has published a detailed, four-phase plan for becoming quantum-resistant, targeting completion by 2028 -- a documented roadmap rather than a vague promise, though nothing on it has shipped yet.

Decentralization is a persistent weak point at 46. The list of roughly 35 validators trusted to secure the network is curated and permissioned -- new validators aren't automatically added, they're chosen -- though the operator base itself is genuinely diverse: exchanges, universities, and individuals across the list, with Ripple itself running only one of the 35 directly.

Privacy & Confidentiality scores 32 -- the ledger is fully transparent today, with no way to hide a transaction. A proposed feature (XLS-0096) that would let certain tokens be transferred confidentially entered formal validator voting after an August 6, 2026 software release, but it would only cover a newer token type called Multi-Purpose Tokens, not XRP itself.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Programmability Tier Partial -- rich native primitives but zero deployable custom logic on mainnet.

key_findings: XRP Ledger only partially passes our programmability check. It has genuinely rich built-in financial features -- a native decentralized exchange, an automated market maker, and escrow -- but there's no way for a developer to deploy custom code on top of it, the way there is on a general-purpose smart-contract chain.

XRP Ledger earns a full pass on our reliability check, having gone twelve consecutive clean months without a qualifying network incident -- proof that our reliability scoring can recover fully to a full pass over time, not just partially.

Economic Predictability is XRP Ledger's strongest category on the AI framework at 85. Transaction fees are fixed and near-zero, with no bidding war for space -- an agent can know its exact cost every time.

watch_items: The proposed confidential-transfer feature (XLS-0096) needs more than 80% validator support sustained for 14 straight days to activate. If it does, it would raise the Privacy & Confidentiality score -- though it would still only cover the newer token type, not XRP itself.
A separate proposed standard (XLS-0101) is also worth watching -- if adopted, it could raise the ceiling on either the finality check or the programmability check.
The CLARITY Act is pending a vote on the Senate floor. If passed, it would move XRP's regulatory standing from informal agency guidance to something written into law.
